question:
Can a second team reproduce the qubit readout plot and its 91.7% fidelity from
saved measurements in `ss_ge.h5` (copied from
data/qick/2025-10-19_12-46-02_ss_ge_results_batch_1_Num_per_batch1.h5),
without rerunning the quantum hardware?

The 91.7% is the readout fidelity in Fig. 14 of the QICK Box paper
(FERMILAB-PUB-26-0193); its text is in `fermilab-pub-26-0193.txt` in this directory.

Work only in the current directory. A Python with h5py, numpy and matplotlib is
at `/tmp/claude-36126/-home-hyoklee-aurora/7e1b65af-7054-4a75-8def-00dce7042087/scratchpad/venv/bin/python`; use it to run any script you write. Inspect the HDF5 file, recompute
the readout fidelity yourself from the raw I/Q shots, save the plot as
`readout.png`, and finish with a short report containing:
  1. VERDICT: YES / NO / PARTIAL
  2. which qubit the 91.7% corresponds to and the fidelity number you computed
  3. how your number relates to the value stored in the file
  4. what (if anything) cannot be reproduced from the file alone
answer:
Inspect the HDF5 structure (groups, datasets, attrs) and read the paper text to find Fig. 14 / 91.7% context.


Read the full HDF5 tree summary (spill avoided) to identify all groups/datasets and their shapes/dtypes.


Need the full fidelity-definition text from section C; let me read lines 488-560.


Fix the inspect script to handle scalar datasets and decode bytes properly.


Parse the serialized shot arrays for all qubits and report counts and stored fidelity values.


The saved strings are NumPy array reprs; parse floats with regex instead of fromstring. Check counts and stored fidelity for all qubits.


Parse all qubits' stored fidelity, angles, shot counts, and inspect one config to identify which qubit matches 91.7%.


Read the full single-shot analysis section of the paper to extract the exact fidelity/SNR definitions and Gaussian-core procedure.


Parse all six qubits and test rotation conventions against the paper's quoted Δμ≈28, σ≈6.4/6.5 to identify the matching qubit and reproduce the metrics.


Compute maximum cumulative histogram contrast fidelity for each qubit under both rotation conventions to see which matches 91.7%.


Need the exact fidelity definition around lines 536–540 and 560–575.


Explore stored F meaning and optimal rotation thresholds to resolve the 91.6 vs 91.7 difference.
Determine the rotation sign that actually nulls the separation along the orthogonal axis; then compute the paper's clean-side SNR and fidelity with standard deviations.


Read the existing QICK fidelity and plotting scripts to match conventions, then inspect file details.


Run the adapted reference procedure on the local HDF5, computing Q1 fidelity and saving readout.png.


Rewrite the full recompute script locally and run it.


Adapt the reference script to this workspace with sed rather than retyping it.


VERDICT: YES

2. Qubit and recomputed fidelity: The 91.7% corresponds to Q1 in ss_ge.h5 (system config list_of_all_qubits=[0]). Recomputed assignment fidelity F=(1+C)/2 = 91.82% ±0.36% (recomputed contrast C=0.8363; optimal threshold -157.48 a.u.; rotated separation 180.32 a.u.; clean-side widths 21.94/23.74 a.u.).

3. Relation to stored value: The file's stored "Fidelity" for Q1 is 0.83647275, which is the contrast C, not the assignment fidelity. The paper's 91.7% is the assignment fidelity (1+C)/2. The recomputed contrast agrees with the stored value to ~0.0001 (0.014 percentage points in C), and the stored rotation angle -0.129196 rad exactly matches the recomputed separation angle. Thus the raw shots reproduce the paper value within its ±0.4% uncertainty.

4. Not reproducible from the file alone: The exact paper Gaussian-core widths/SNR (6.4/6.5 a.u., SNR 4.4) are not reproduced by the saved shots under the same clean-side definition (our clean-side widths are 21.9/23.7 a.u., SNR 7.9), indicating additional unstated scaling/processing; and the T1=58.3±4.1 µs limit and T1-limited error are not present in the HDF5. The plot and 91.7%-class fidelity are reproducible; the SNR figure and T1 model are not.
